The way i resolved the issue is by running linux as a main system, with two win 10 VMs (one for gaming, one for work).

You can pick any distro you like. I'd suggest Gentoo (my personal favorite) if you want to poke around the system, Debian or Mint if you just want it to work.

Get yourself a copy of windows 10, ideally enterprise LTSB. That version is meant for corporate boxes, it doesn't have any of the godawful shit they introduced in 10 like cortana or windows store. Put that system into a VM (i use KVM/QEMU), and you'll be good to go on work stuff.

With this setup you can use linux for everything, should you need windows for anything, just alt tab into the VM and do what you need. I have enough ram so i just keep it running at all times, works like a charm and is great to work with.

For gaming, it's the same thing except slightly more complicated as you need a PCI passthrough. Fairly easy to setup with the guides that are available, but it requires some extra hardware. You'll need two GPUs, one for your main box, the other that'll be isolated and passed directly to the VM. First one can be anything as you don't need any real power to render a desktop, second one should be whatever gaming GPU you're comfortable with (i'm running an old gtx760 for linux, gtx1070 for the VM).

With this you'll be able to play games in the VM at near native performance. It helps to have a monitor with two inputs you can flip between easily, since you'll have a cable from each card plugged into the monitor.

To summarize it, yes it's possible to run linux as a main and still have access to everything you need out of windows, though it might cost you a bit extra to do it properly. I suggest 2 separate ssds (1 linux, 1 gaming vm), 2 gpus (one for desktop, one for gaming), and 32 gigs of ram.
